Residents along the Budhi Gandaki and Trishuli river corridors have been strictly advised to move away from riverbanks and stay on high ground. videos.caption: 🔴 Inundación masiva en Nepal, de nuevo. Una nueva riada golpea este domingo el distrito de Gorkha, en el centro-norte de Nepal. La crecida repentina del río Budhi Gandaki arrasa unas 40 viviendas y varios puentes y deja al menos cinco desaparecidos.El agua también daña instalaciones eléctricas, torres de comunicaciones y las obras de una central hidroeléctrica. El Ejército moviliza helicópteros y equipos terrestres y comunica el rescate de 49 personas. Las autoridades envían unos 200.000 mensajes de alerta para pedir evacuaciones ante el riesgo de nuevas crecidas. Las primeras investigaciones apuntan a un desprendimiento que bloqueó temporalmente un afluente: al romperse la barrera natural, una enorme masa de agua y lodo se precipitó río abajo. Los registros meteorológicos no muestran lluvias en las cabeceras que expliquen la inundación. La emergencia llega cuando Nepal todavía se recupera de las devastadoras inundaciones de agosto, que dejaron más de 1.400 muertos y miles de desaparecidos cerca de la frontera con China. El Gobierno había anunciado esta semana el fin de la búsqueda activa de víctimas de aquella catástrofe para concentrar los recursos en la reconstrucción de las zonas afectadas. 📲 ¡Síguenos para estar al tanto de la actualidad! #inundacion #ultimahora #breaking #nepal #viral

Longsor diduga menyumbat aliran sungai atau anak sungai, kemudian memicu luapan air secara mendadak. Laporan The Kathmandu Post memperkirakan sekitar 35–40 rumah hanyut dan beberapa jembatan rusak atau hancur. Lokasi pembangunan proyek pembangkit listrik tenaga air juga terdampak. Lima orang dilaporkan hilang dalam laporan Reuters, sementara 49 orang berhasil diselamatkan oleh tim militer Nepal. Data korban masih dapat berubah seiring proses pencarian. Sebelumnya pada Rabu, 26 Agustus 2026, banjir bandang dahsyat menerjang Distrik Rasuwa, Nepal, dan berdampak pada sejumlah wilayah di sepanjang aliran Sungai Bhote Koshi dan Trishuli. Laporan awal Radio Nepal pada 26 Agustus mencatat 95 korban meninggal yang telah ditemukan atau terkonfirmasi saat itu. Angka tersebut merupakan data pada tahap awal penanganan bencana. Nepal is once again facing a devastating flood disaster in the Budhigandaki region, causing widespread destruction to hundreds of homes and buildings, damaging major bridges, and disrupting vital road networks connecting key districts. What makes this tragedy even more heartbreaking is that Nepal has barely had time to recover from the recent floods in the Bhotekoshi rasuwa and Trishuli river regions. Now, we are facing yet another disaster, leaving communities displaced, infrastructure damaged, livelihoods destroyed, and countless families living in uncertainty. At this point, we must ask ourselves: How many more disasters must Nepal endure before long-term solutions become a national and international priority? It is true that floods are natural disasters, and no country can completely prevent them. We should not rush to blame any single individual or institution for the forces of nature. However, the scale of destruction, the repeated loss of infrastructure, and the vulnerability of communities raise serious questions about preparedness, disaster-risk management, infrastructure planning, and climate resilience.                                         This is where geopolitics and international cooperation must move beyond diplomatic statements and deliver practical results. Nepal should strengthen regional cooperation with India, China, Bangladesh, and other relevant partners, while using international platforms such as the G20 to advocate for climate finance, disaster-resilient infrastructure, technology transfer, and stronger regional early-warning mechanisms. #prayfornepal #fyp #flood #nepal #budigandaki

According to Nepalese media reports citing local authorities, the flood destroyed the bridge connecting parts of Aarughat Rural Municipality, along with other bridges and homes. A suspected landslide blocked a stream before water surged downstream, although authorities are still assessing the circumstances and the full extent of the damage.  Emergency teams have been deployed, and residents in vulnerable riverside areas have been warned to move to higher ground. Reports differ on the number of people missing, with at least four reported missing in one update. While many people were still searching for their missing loved ones after the devastating floods in August, another tragedy struck the country. Five people were reported missing, and 49 were rescued as emergency teams monitored the danger. But the most heartbreaking part is that this nightmare comes while Nepal is still struggling to recover from an earlier catastrophe that left more than 1,400 people dead and thousands unaccounted for. 🚨Shocking visuals coming from Nepal's Gorkha District today. A massive, black debris-filled flood surged down the Budhi Gandaki River early this morning after a landslide blocked the river in Chumnubri village. The temporary dam suddenly burst, unleashing a wall of water, mud and rocks. In the video you can see entire buildings with green roofs being swallowed in seconds as people watch helplessly from the hilltop. According to authorities, more than 35-65 houses in Salleri Bazaar, Jagat, Paiyuka and riverbed settlements have been swept away. At least 4 bridges including 2 motorable bridges were destroyed. 5 to 10 people are reported missing so far, and 49 people have been rescued and airlifted by the Nepal Army. A RED ALERT has been issued for downstream districts - Gorkha, Tanahun, Chitwan, Nawalparasi. Residents are being urged to stay away from the river and move to high ground. This comes just 2 months after the deadly August flood in Nepal that killed over 1,400 people. Pray for Nepal. 🙏 #NepalFlood #PrayForNepal #Gorkha #FlashFlood #NepalNews
